title: The Saturday Shift
text:
Nurul did not choose to volunteer at the food distribution centre. Her school required a certain number of service hours, and this was the only slot left.
The work was less inspiring than she had imagined. There were no speeches and no photographs, only a long trestle table and hundreds of identical bags to be packed with rice, oil and tinned food. Her arms ached within the hour.
What she remembers now is not the packing, but an elderly man who came to collect his bag and stayed to ask about her examinations. He told her, quite seriously, that she should sleep more. Then he thanked her and walked slowly home.
She has gone back every Saturday since. Nobody requires it of her any longer.
